subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw make periodic memory sync a default-on fallback for unconfigured memorySearch users, or keep interval sync opt-in while relying on watcher hardening and manual indexing?
rationale: The remaining fix is small in code but changes fallback/default behavior for existing users, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive and maintainer-owned.

options.title: Accept a scoped default fallback
options.body: Land or sponsor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90019 or a successor after resolving the dirty-source scoping and documenting the 30-minute default/0 opt-out.

options.title: Keep interval sync opt-in
options.body: Close or narrow the linked PR to docs and rely on current watcher hardening plus explicit `intervalMinutes` configuration for users who want periodic rescans.

options.title: Add diagnostics first
options.body: Keep the default at 0 and add warning, status, or doctor detection for stalled memory freshness before changing runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Accept a scoped default fallback
recommendation.body: Land or sponsor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90019 or a successor after resolving the dirty-source scoping and documenting the 30-minute default/0 opt-out.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core/config history and current area ownership make this the best available owner for the default/fallback decision.
